changesSinceV1: All 8 Global color ramps expanded from 5 steps to 12 steps each (0/50/100/200/300/400/500/600/700/800/900/950), including neutral (11->12 steps).

Dark mode rebuilt on request: every Theme token that referenced the neutral ramp in Dark mode (24 tokens - all surfaces, text, icons, borders, dividers) now references the brand ramp instead, so dark mode is genuinely built on the primary brand color, not a neutral tone.

Every dark-mode pairing re-verified against real WCAG contrast math after the swap; 7 of the 24 tokens needed a lighter brand step than the direct numeric equivalent to stay compliant (documented per-token below via the ref field).

A full sweep for same-value collisions within semantic token families found 19 instances; 17 were resolved with WCAG-checked distinct values, 2 were left alone deliberately (Light-mode surface default/raised pairs, which use Effect Styles/shadow for differentiation instead of color).
Fixed a genuine pre-existing WCAG failure surfaced during that sweep: text/tertiary and icon/tertiary in Light mode were failing contrast entirely (2.76:1, below even the 3.0 floor) - now resolved.
openItems: All color hex values are pending final brand confirmation - the underlying hue choices (neutral, brand, semantic ramps) trace back to a pixel-sampled reference image, not an authoritative brand export. The 12-step expansion and dark-mode rework are structurally complete and WCAG-verified, but not yet brand-team sign-off.
Warning and Info color ramps are WCAG-derived (contrast-verified against actual usage pairings), not brand-confirmed.
Icon set/family is not represented in this JSON at all - icon sizing tokens exist (global.icon.*) but no specific icon library is endorsed here.
High-contrast mode is structurally unaddressed - no separate mode exists in Theme beyond Light/Dark.
Component-tier tokens under 'button.Tertiary' and 'button.ghost' currently coexist and resolve to identical values - consolidation to a single canonical name is a pending decision.

feedback/*/text and feedback/*/border (and the equivalent status/* pairs) intentionally share the same value in several cases - confirmed as a deliberate, consistent pattern (cohesive alert styling), not an oversight.
